_comment: Test-timing diagnostic thresholds for scripts/test_timing_check.py. tolerance: a baselined test is flagged when it runs slower than tolerance x its baseline time AND by at least min_regression_delta seconds in absolute terms. absolute_ceiling: every ordinary-PR test is reported when it runs longer than this many seconds, whether or not it is baselined. min_regression_delta: the absolute slowdown floor (seconds) below which a multiplicative 'regression' is treated as scheduler/contention jitter and not flagged -- most of the baseline is near-zero (~0.00-0.01s), so without this floor a few-millisecond jitter floods reports for unchanged tests on a contended runner. Hosted CI uses --informational because repeated unchanged-code samples crossed both thresholds; invalid telemetry still fails closed. All three are config so the diagnostic moves without code changes.
